description.narrative:
The activity will contribute to the implementation of the regional Action Plan for LAC region (2023-2029), specifically in the Caribbean SIDS, by focusing on conservation, risk management and preparedness and the update of Tentative Lists through capacity-building, technical advice and participatory processes.
Activities under this workplan aim at strengthening capacities of World Heritage sites’ managers and National Focal Points in the Caribbean, while promoting the integration of disaster risk reduction, preparedness and response mechanisms in existing management plans of selected World Heritage sites, thus contributing to respond to the most pressing challenges faced by heritage properties, as well as following-up to the ‘Caribbean Plan of Action for Disaster Resilience and Recovery of the Culture sector’ in partnership with CARICOM and CDEMA. Similarly, they will aim at enhancing cultural and natural heritage protection through awareness-raising and educational initiatives, particularly targeting young people and local communities who live within and around prioritized World Heritage sites.
In this regard, the implementation strategy will aim at addressing existing challenges and priorities building on the results achieved and the lessons learned during previous biennia, and will respond to the main priority set by the World Heritage Committee, which focuses on the conservation of sites already inscribed in the World Heritage List, and the protection of their Outsanding Universal Value. On another hand, UNESCO’s efforts under this workplan will be aligned with following regional strategic lines of action established by the Action Plan for World Heritage in Latin America and the Caribbean (2023-2029).
